chunks: And from him, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Isa ibn Sabih, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the pickpocket, the grave-robber, and the snatcher. He said: “His hand is not cut off.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the authority being asked for the ruling
key_terms.لَا يُقْطَعُ: the hadd of hand-cutting is not carried out in this case
key_terms.ٱلطَّرَّارِ: a pickpocket who steals stealthily from a person's possession
key_terms.ٱلنَّبَّاشِ: a grave-robber who digs up graves to take what is buried
key_terms.ٱلْمُخْتَلِسِ: a snatcher who quickly seizes property openly and flees

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment of hand-cutting apply to a pickpocket, grave-robber, or snatcher in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام regarding certain forms of theft-related misconduct. It states that the fixed hadd punishment of cutting off the hand is not applied to the pickpocket, the grave-robber, and the snatcher mentioned in the report.
